part.name: BBa_26TOGLX3
part.title: SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag
part.description: This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4*;* the wild-type acdS sequence is registered as [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi).  It is an enzyme commonly found in plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of the plant hormone ethylene, thereby alleviating ethylene-induced growth inhibition in plants under stress. The ACC deaminase protein is fused to the alpha-amylase signal peptide (SamyQ) at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS:[ <u>BBa\_26MA70QI</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a translational fusion with three elements, in this order:

1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
2. **AcdS 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_262YYNPV**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-262yynpv)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida* *(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303) , with its native start codon and stop codon removed  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from AcdS wild-type ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.

The complete part was obtained by de novo gene synthesis.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 
* **Main purpose of use:** Expression and secretion of ACC deaminase in the host *B. subtilis* 
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants

## Dry lab / computational analysis

The mRNA secondary structure around the ribosome binding site and start codon heavily influences the translation-initiation efficiency inside bacteria. Synonymous codons, meaning codons that result in the same amino acids, in the 5' end of a CDS can impact how the mRNA folds near the binding site. The folding can either hide or expose the Shine Dalgarno sequence and start codon, impacting the efficiency of ribosome binding and translation initiation. Following this concept suggested by Castillo-Hair (2019), the design pipeline treated the first 15 codons of the acdS CDS as an editable region. ViennaRNA 2.7.2 was used to generate and fold tens of thousands of synonymous variants in the RS-inclusive 236-nt 5' window (residual recombination site + MF001 RBS + spacer + SamyQ ORF + first 90 nt of cds), determining the mean base-pair unpaired probability across the 15 nt following the ATG and across the MF001 Shine-Dalgarno core (AAGGAGG) and creating a balance score.

SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag was determined to be the best candidate from the run: 12 of the first 15 acdS codons were changed (c2 TTA→TTG, c3 AAT→AAC, c4 AGA→CGC, c7 AGA→CGC, c8 TAT→TAC, c9 CCG→CCC, c10 TTA→CTT, c11 ACA→ACT, c12 TTC→TTT, c13 GGA→GGG, c14 CCG→CCA, c15 AGC→AGT). The predicted start+15 accessibility improved from 0.563 to 0.773 and SD-core accessibility improved from 0.088 to 0.203 when compared to the wild type, resulting in an overall balance score gain of 0.651 to 0.976. The codon adaptation index against B. subtilis 168 usage dropped from 0.85 to 0.75. Instead of following Castillo's rule, which prioritizes low GC content and A over U, the program individually folded and verified every candidate to verify improved accessibility, as the Castillo-rule-applied control produced a start+15 score of only 0.698 and an SD-core score of 0.186 (balance 0.884), which, although still an improvement over wild type, remained lower than the balance achieved through individual verification of every candidate.

## Literature

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

The SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag coding sequence was amplified by PCR and cloned into a pSTK-0C-sfGFP vector from the SubtiToolKit provided by [<u>**Dr. Joaquín Caro-Astorga**</u>](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F11jg8gn6cr\&q=Dr.+Joaqu%C3%ADn+Caro-Astorga), giving pSTK-0C-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1. The ligation was transformed into *E. coli* strain DH5α, and positive clones carrying the SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag coding sequence were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing to confirm the insert before use in subsequent Golden Gate reactions.

* **Insert:** SamyQ signal peptide – AcdS 2.1 – 6x Histag, \[1122 bp]
* **Amplification primers:** 

| Primer name | Primer sequence (5’ to 3’)                         |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| SamyQ F     | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGA TTCAAAAACGAAAGCGGAC |
| ACCD R      | ATATATGAAGACATGAGGGGTCTCATG TCTTAATGATGATGATGATGAT |

* **Annealing temperature:** 60°C
* **Template:** synthetized fragment
* **Vector:** pSTK-0C-sfGFP (chloramphenicol resistance) The plasmid contains a superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) cassette, flanked by Type IIS restriction sites, that serves as a visual selection marker; cells containing the empty vector therefore become fluoresce green, while successful insertion of the target DNA fragment replaces the sfGFP sequence, resulting in white/non-fluorescent colonies.

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-0C-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag transformation were screened by colony PCR with the SamyQ and STK primers, which flank the insertion site. The products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder to assess cloning success. A correct band runs at the expected size, which is the length of the SamyQ-AcdS-Histag insert \[1122 bp] plus the vector sequence between the Histag and STK R priming site, for a total of \[1331 bp]. A band at this size confirms that a fragment of the correct length was ligated into the vector at the expected position. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates for the correct insert.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the insert is free of mutations and that the signal peptide, AcdS coding sequence, and Histag. Clones with a verified sequence were used for the Level 1 Golden Gate reactions.

documentation.title: Application
documentation.value:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26XVQ3FS**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xvq3fs)): this **Protectant Module** constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS, and terminator B0015.
* **PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26DE5E2Q**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26de5e2q)): this module includes the light-responsive promoter P*cpcG2*-veg, the RBS EEBD-RBS0, a protectant CDS, and the terminator B0015, which together drive the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in *Bacillus Subtilis* after[ <u>BBa\_26XZYM10</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10),[ <u>BBa\_261XH2RS</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs), and[ <u>BBa\_26BDO8AQ</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq).
* **ccaSR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag** ([<u>**BBa\_26U8UTMH**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26u8utmh)): the system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control.
